title: Archaeologists discover 600-year-old Christian monastery in Germany
content: The thick monastery walls were preserved beneath rubble that collected over the centuries. A development project in the town center of Borken, in western Germany, revealed the well-preserved remains of a monastery. The brick foundation was over five feet tall in some places, and it was buried under thick layers of rubble. Archaeologists working on a preventive dig ahead of a construction project in the German town of Borken, near the Dutch border, discovered a remarkable piece of history. The red brick foundations and thick walls of the church, which were bound by lime mortar, are well-preserved despite the passing of the centuries. The walls were four feet thick and over five feet tall, often buried beneath layers of thick rubble that helped preserve the ancient foundation as the city grew and expanded over it. Hidden away in the hills of Austria, just outside the city of Vienna, is Heiligenkreuz Abbey. Dating back to 1133, it is the oldest continuous Cistercian abbey in the world. EWTN's Colm Flynn gets a rare look inside the abbey, where visitors are not normally permitted, and meets one of the monks who has dedicated their life to daily prayer and worship.

title: Medieval monastery remains discovered beneath Borken's ...
content: # Medieval monastery remains discovered beneath Borken’s historic center in Germany. Archaeologists have been working for months in the historic center of Borken, where a new health center and Caritas building are planned in the Brinkerhof quarter. The highlight of the preliminary investigations: the massive and well-preserved foundations of the church of the former Marienbrink Monastery from the Late Middle Ages. During this phase, archaeologists encountered the first clear remains of the former Marienbrink Monastery church. In 2024, the team identified a World War II air raid bunker southwest of the church remains. In 1818, a synagogue with an adjoining school and a mikveh was established on the grounds, reusing parts of the older complex.
